validity.recommendation: no action -- existence, classification and route all independently corroborated; keep as-is
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE all clean. Crossroads Pipeline Company is a real, long-standing FERC-jurisdictional interstate gas transmission line, confirmed independently of the wiki page and of GEM: (1) TC Energy's own current operations page (tcenergy.com/operations/natural-gas/crossroads-pipeline/) states '202 miles (365 km)' operating in Indiana and Ohio, FERC-regulated, operator TC Energy. (2) SEC EDGAR full-text search turns up 'Crossroads Pipeline Company' (Indiana incorporation) as a named consolidated subsidiary in NiSource Inc.'s Exhibit 21 subsidiary lists every year 2001-2015 (checked the 2014 filing directly: listed under 'COLUMBIA PIPELINE GROUP OPERATIONS' alongside Columbia Gas Transmission and Columbia Gulf Transmission) -- an origin fully independent of TC Energy. (3) Columbia Pipeline Group, Inc.'s own FY2016 10-K (CIK 1629995, filed 2017-02-17, a distinct SEC filer from TC Energy) lists Crossroads as one of its consolidated subsidiaries and gives annual throughput of 16.7 / 15.5 / 15.5 MMDth for 2014/2015/2016 -- i.e. gas was actually moving through the line every one of those years, which is itself direct, dated, independent evidence of 'operating' status (context-based per the status-inference rule), not merely a name check. (4) The gem.wiki page's own harvested citation pool led to a contemporary 1993 Northwest Indiana Times article ('NIPSCO to convert pipeline', Sep 3 1993) -- read in full (the site ROT47-obfuscates article body text server-side; decoded by hand, confirmed live at 200 -- url_verifier's substring screen misses the value because the raw response is still encoded, so name_found is hand-confirmed here, not automated). It independently states: 'The 202-mile pipeline, formerly owned by Tecumseh Pipe Line Co., has been used since it was built in 1957 to transport crude oil to Indiana and Ohio refineries. The pipeline, now called Crossroads, runs from Schererville to [northwest Ohio].' This predates GEM/gem.wiki by decades and independently corroborates the 202-mile length, the Schererville origin, and the Indiana-to-northwest-Ohio route (consistent with the sheet's Cygnet, OH endpoint -- Cygnet is in Wood County, in northwest Ohio). Classification as a gas TRANSMISSION trunk (not gathering/local) is correct -- it is FERC-jurisdictional interstate pipe per TC Energy's own page. No duplicate: checked the full 46-row roster: no other row shares Schererville, Cygnet, or a Crossroads-adjacent corridor; Rover/NEXUS/Columbia Gas Transmission/etc. all run different corridors. Open item (not a concern, just unverified): Capacity=300 MMcf/d appears on gem.wiki but I could not find an independent primary source stating that number -- TC Energy's page gives length only, not capacity; CPG's 10-K gives actual throughput (15.5 MMDth/yr =~ 42 MMcf/d average), which is well below a 300 MMcf/d nameplate and does not contradict it, but doesn't confirm the exact figure either. Diameter and Pressure remain genuinely unsourced (see fills, both UNRESOLVED) -- FERC eLibrary's docket search is a JS app that does not respond to scripted GET, EIA's 1998 report link (webapp1.dlib.indiana.edu) now serves a Cloudflare human-verification challenge and its retrieval path resolves only to a library catalog card, not the actual PDF, and the harvested naturalgasintel.com article 404s (page removed/renumbered, not found via Wayback either) -- these would be the next things to chase for diameter/pressure.

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's StartYear1=1995 (unsourced, MISSING_REF) is in tension with the contemporary primary account. The 1993 NWI Times article (see above; hand-decoded, live, names the pipeline) lays out the conversion in two phases: Phase 1 (140 mi within Indiana) 'will begin Tuesday' (the article ran Sep 3, 1993) and 'By Nov. 1 it will be helping [NIPSCO] supply gas' -- i.e. Phase 1 targeted for the 1993-94 winter heating season. Phase 2 (the remaining 62 mi in Ohio) 'will begin in the first quarter of 1994; it will be completed by the 1994 winter heating season' -- i.e. full completion targeted for roughly Oct/Nov 1994, not 1995. gem.wiki (read for leads only, not cited) states 1995, which is presumably where the sheet's value originated, but that is a retrospective claim with no citation of its own on the wiki page for that specific year. I could not resolve the ~1-year gap with a second source in the time available: FERC eLibrary's docket search does not respond to a scripted GET (JS app), the EIA 1998 report link that might carry an as-built in-service date is blocked by a Cloudflare challenge, and naturalgasintel.com's 1998 sign-up article 404s. Flagging as a spec concern rather than silently accepting 1995: the 1994-completion account is contemporaneous trade/local reporting (arguably more reliable on execution timing than a source-less retrospective wiki claim), but 'winter heating season' language could plausibly stretch into early 1995, so this is not a slam-dunk -- recommend Baird or a follow-up pull the FERC docket (this is FERC-jurisdictional per TC Energy) for the actual in-service order/certificate date before changing the cell.
